Main.sentence: During ___E:presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election)___ campaigns in the United States, it has become customary for the candidates to engage in one or more ___E:debates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debate)___ .

The topics discussed in the debate are often the most ___E:controversial U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Controversial)___ issues of the time, and arguably elections have been nearly decided by these debates.
Candidate debates are not ___E:constitutionally U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Constitution)___ mandated, but they are now considered an intrinsic part of the election process.

The debates are targeted mainly at ___E:undecided voters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undecided_voters)___ ; those who tend not to be partial to any ___E:political ideology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_ideologies_in_the_United_States)___ or ___E:party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_parties_in_the_United_States)___ .

Presidential debates are typically held late in the ___E:election cycle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Election_cycle)___ , after the political parties have ___E:nominated their candidates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_nominating_convention)___ .
The candidates typically meet in a large hall, often at a university, and usually before an audience of citizens.

The formats of the debates have varied, with questions sometimes posed from one or more journalist ___E:moderators U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discussion_moderator)___ and in other cases members of the audience.

The debate formats established during the ___E:1988 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_United_States_presidential_election)___ through ___E:2000 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election)___ campaigns were governed in detail by secret ___E:memoranda of understanding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorandum_of_understanding)___ (MOU) between the two major candidates; the MOU for the ___E:2004 debates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_presidential_debates)___ was, unlike the earlier agreements, jointly released to the public by the participants.

Debates have been broadcast live on television, radio, and in recent years, the web. The ___E:first debate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_United_States_presidential_debates)___ for the ___E:1960 election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_United_States_presidential_election)___ drew over 66 million viewers out of a population of 179 million, making it one of the ___E:most-watched broadcasts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-watched_television_broadcasts)___ in U.S. television history.
The ___E:1980 debates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_United_States_presidential_debates)___ drew 80 million viewers out of a population of 226 million.

Recent debates have drawn smaller audiences, ranging from 46 million for the first ___E:2000 debate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_debates)___ to a high of over 67 million for the first ___E:debate in 2012 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_presidential_debates)___ .

A record-breaking audience of over 84 million people watched the first ___E:2016 presidential debate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_United_States_presidential_debates)___ between ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ and ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ , a number that does not reflect online streaming.
Since 1960, no year has had more than three presidential debates.
The first general presidential debate was not held until 1960, but several other debates are considered predecessors to the presidential debates.

The series of seven debates in 1858 between ___E:Abraham Lincoln U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln)___ and ___E:Senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ ___E:Stephen A. Douglas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_A._Douglas)___ for U.S.

Senate were true, face-to-face debates, with no moderator; the candidates took it in turns to open each debate with a one-hour speech, then the other candidate had an hour and a half to rebut, and finally the first candidate closed the debate with a half-hour response.
Douglas was later re-elected to the U.S.
Senate by the Illinois legislature.

Lincoln and Douglas were both nominated for president in 1860 by the ___E:Republicans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1860_Republican_National_Convention)___ and ___E:Northern Democrats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Democrats)___ , respectively, and their earlier debates helped define their respective positions in that election, but they did not meet during the ___E:1860 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1860_United_States_presidential_election)___ .

___E:Wendell Willkie U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendell_Willkie)___ became the first 20th century presidential candidate to challenge his opponent to a face to face debate when in ___E:1940 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1940_United_States_presidential_election)___ he challenged President ___E:Franklin D. Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt)___ , but Roosevelt refused. [citation needed] In 1948, presidential candidate debates became a reality when a ___E:radio debate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewey%E2%80%93Stassen_debate)___ was held in ___E:Oregon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon)___ between Republicans ___E:Thomas E. Dewey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_E._Dewey)___ and ___E:Harold Stassen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Stassen)___ during the party's presidential ___E:primary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partisan_primary)___ .

The Democrats followed suit in 1956 with a televised presidential primary debate between ___E:Adlai Stevenson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adlai_Stevenson_II)___ and ___E:Estes Kefauver U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estes_Kefauver)___ ,   and in 1960 by one between ___E:John F. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy)___ and ___E:Hubert Humphrey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubert_Humphrey)___ .

In 1956, during the ___E:1956 presidential campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_United_States_presidential_election)___ , ___E:University of Maryland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Maryland,_College_Park)___ student Fred Kahn led an effort to bring the two major presidential candidates, ___E:Adlai Stevenson II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adlai_Stevenson_II)___ , the Democratic nominee, and President ___E:Dwight Eisenhower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Eisenhower)___ , the Republican nominee, to the campus for a debate.
Various newspapers were contacted and numerous letters were sent in an effort to generate interest and garner support for the proposal.

Former ___E:first lady U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_the_United_States)___ ___E:Eleanor Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eleanor_Roosevelt)___ was among those who received a letter.

Kahn later told ___E:Guy Raz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Raz)___ during an All Things Considered interview on ___E:NPR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR)___ in 2012 that she replied, saying, "not only would the students of the University of Maryland be interested, but also other students." Roosevelt said that she was going to forward Kahn's letter to ___E:James Finnegan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_A._Finnegan)___ , Adlai Stevenson's ___E:campaign manager U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campaign_manager)___ .

In the end, no debate took place, but Kahn's effort received national press exposure, helping lay groundwork for the ___E:Kennedy–Nixon debates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_United_States_presidential_debates)___ four years later during the ___E:1960 presidential campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_United_States_presidential_election)___ .

The first general election presidential debate was ___E:1960 United States presidential debates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_United_States_presidential_debates)___ , held on September 26, 1960, between Senator ___E:John F. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy)___ , the Democratic nominee, and Vice President ___E:Richard Nixon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon)___ , the Republican nominee, at ___E:CBS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS)___ 's ___E:WBBM-TV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WBBM-TV)___ in ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ .

It was moderated by ___E:Howard K. Smith U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_K._Smith)___ and included a panel composed of ___E:Sander Vanocur U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sander_Vanocur)___ of ___E:NBC News U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC_News)___ , Charles Warren of ___E:Mutual News U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutual_News)___ , ___E:Stuart Novins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Novins)___ of CBS, and Bob Fleming of ___E:ABC News U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_(United_States))___ .
At the outset, Nixon was considered to have the upper hand due to his knowledge of foreign policy and proficiency in radio debates.

However, because of his unfamiliarity with the new format of televised debates, factors such as his underweight and pale appearance, his suit color blending in with the debate set background, and his refusal to use television makeup resulting in a five o'clock shadow, led to his defeat.
Many observers have regarded Kennedy's win [neutrality is disputed] over Nixon in the first debate as a turning point in the election.
After the first debate, polls showed Kennedy moving from a slight deficit into a slight lead over Nixon.

Three more debates were subsequently held between the candidates:  on October 7 at the ___E:WRC-TV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WRC-TV)___ NBC studio in ___E:Washington, D.C. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C.)___ , narrated by ___E:Frank McGee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_McGee_(journalist))___ with a panel of four newsmen ___E:Paul Niven U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_K._Niven_Jr.)___ of CBS, ___E:Edward P. Morgan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_P._Morgan)___ of ABC, Alvin Spivak of ___E:United Press International U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Press_International)___ ,  and Harold R. Levy of Newsday , on October 13, with Nixon at the ABC studio in ___E:Los Angeles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles)___ and Kennedy at the ABC studio in ___E:New York City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City)___ , narrated by ___E:Bill Shadel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Shadel)___ with a panel of four newsmen in a different Los Angeles studio; and October 21 at the ABC studio in New York, narrated by ___E:Quincy Howe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quincy_Howe)___ with a panel of four including Frank Singiser, John Edwards, ___E:Walter Cronkite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Cronkite)___ , and ___E:John Chancellor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Chancellor)___ .

Nixon regained his lost weight, wore television makeup, and appeared more forceful than in his initial appearance, winning the second and third debates while the fourth was a draw, [neutrality is disputed] however the viewership numbers of these subsequent events did not match the high set by the first debate and ultimately did not help Nixon as he lost the election.

After the Kennedy–Nixon debates, it was 16 years before general election presidential candidates again debated each other face to face. During this interval intra-party debates were held during the ___E:1968 Democratic primaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Democratic_Party_presidential_primaries)___ , between ___E:Robert F. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy)___ and ___E:Eugene McCarthy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugene_McCarthy)___ , and again during the ___E:1972 Democratic primaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Democratic_Party_presidential_primaries)___ , between ___E:George McGovern U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_McGovern)___ , ___E:Hubert Humphrey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubert_Humphrey)___ , and others. [citation needed]

The next presidential candidates debates occurred during the ___E:1976 campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_United_States_presidential_election)___ , when President ___E:Gerald Ford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford)___ , who had entered office two years earlier after President ___E:Richard Nixon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon)___ resigned, agreed to three debates with his Democratic challenger, ___E:Jimmy Carter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter)___ .

The ___E:1976 debates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_United_States_presidential_debates)___ , one on domestic issues, one on foreign policy, and one on any topic, were held before studio audiences, and, like the 1960 debates, were televised nationally.
The ___E:League of Women Voters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Women_Voters)___ sponsored the debates.
This was a change from the Kennedy–Nixon debates, which had been sponsored by the television networks themselves.

Roughly an hour into the first televised debate, the broadcast audio coming from the ___E:Walnut Street Theatre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walnut_Street_Theatre)___ and fed to all networks suddenly cut out, effectively muting the candidates in the middle of a statement by Carter.
The two candidates were initially unaware of this technical glitch and continued to debate, unheard to the television audience.

They were soon informed of this problem, and proceeded to stand still and silently at their lecterns for about 27 minutes, until the problem, a blown ___E:capacitor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capacitor)___ , was located and fixed, in time for Carter to briefly finish the statement he had begun when the audio cut out, and for both candidates to issue closing statements.
The dramatic effect of televised presidential debates was demonstrated again in the 1976 debates between Ford and Carter.
Ford had already cut into Carter's large lead in the polls, and was generally viewed as having won the first debate on domestic policy.

Polls released after this first debate indicated the race was even. However, in the second debate on foreign policy, Ford made what was widely viewed as a major blunder when he said "There is no ___E:Soviet domination of Eastern Europe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Bloc)___ and there never will be under a Ford administration." After this, Ford's momentum stalled, and Carter won a very close election.

The League of Women Voters also sponsored the debates held in ___E:1980 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_United_States_presidential_debates)___ and in ___E:1984 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_United_States_presidential_debates)___ .
In 1980, debates were a major factor again.
Earlier in the election season, President Carter held a substantial lead over his opponents.

Three debates between ___E:Carter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter)___ , former California Governor ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ and ___E:Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois)___ Congressman ___E:John B. Anderson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_B._Anderson)___ (who was running as an independent), were originally scheduled; along with a single vice presidential debate between incumbent ___E:Walter Mondale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Mondale)___ , former ___E:CIA Director U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_the_Central_Intelligence_Agency)___ ___E:George Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush)___ , and former ___E:Wisconsin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin)___ Governor ___E:Patrick Joseph Lucey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Joseph_Lucey)___ .

Carter refused to debate if Anderson was present and Reagan refused to debate without Anderson, resulting in the first debate being between Reagan and Anderson only. The second debate and the vice presidential debate were both cancelled.
Reagan eventually conceded to Carter's demand, and a single debate took place with only Carter and Reagan.
With years of experience in front of a camera as an actor, Reagan came across much better than Carter in the debate and was judged by voters to have won by a wide margin.
Reagan's debate performance likely helped propel his landslide victory in the general election.

The Reagan campaign had access to internal debate briefing materials for Carter; the exposure of this in 1983 led to a public scandal called " ___E:Debategate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debategate)___ ". [citation needed]
In 1984, former Vice President Walter Mondale won the first debate over President Ronald Reagan, generating much-needed donations to Mondale's lagging campaign.
The second presidential debate was held on October 21, 1984, where Ronald Reagan used a joke, "I will not make age an issue of this campaign.
I am not going to exploit, for political purposes, my opponent's youth and inexperience", which effectively stalled Mondale's momentum. [citation needed]
Since 1976, each presidential election has featured a series of presidential debates.
Vice presidential debates have been held regularly since 1984. Vice Presidential debates have been largely uneventful and have historically had little impact on the election.

Perhaps the most memorable moment in a vice presidential debate came in the 1988 debate between Republican ___E:Dan Quayle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Quayle)___ and Democrat ___E:Lloyd Bentsen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Bentsen)___ .

Quayle's selection by the incumbent vice-president and Republican presidential candidate ___E:George Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush)___ was widely criticized; one reason being his relative lack of experience.

In the debate, Quayle attempted to ease this fear by stating that he had as much experience as John F. Kennedy did when he ran for president in 1960. Democrat Bentsen countered with the now famous statement: "Senator, I served with Jack Kennedy.
I knew Jack Kennedy.
Jack Kennedy was a friend of mine. ___E:Senator, you're no Jack Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senator,_you%27re_no_Jack_Kennedy)___ ."

In 1992, the first debate was held involving both major party candidates and a third-party candidate, billionaire ___E:Ross Perot U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Perot)___ , running against President Bush and the Democratic nominee ___E:Governor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Arkansas)___ ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ .
That year, President Bush was criticized for his early hesitation to join the debates, and some described him as a "chicken".

Furthermore, he was criticized for looking at his watch which aides initially said was meant to track if the other candidates were debating within their time limits but ultimately it was revealed that the president indeed was checking how much time was left in the debate.

Moderators of nationally televised presidential debates have included ___E:Bernard Shaw U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Shaw_(journalist))___ , ___E:Bill Moyers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Moyers)___ , ___E:Jim Lehrer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Lehrer)___ , and ___E:Barbara Walters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Walters)___ .

___E:Saint Anselm College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Anselm_College)___ has hosted four primary debates throughout 2004 and 2008; it is a favorite for campaign stops and these national debates because of the college's history in the ___E:New Hampshire primary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire_primary)___ .

___E:Washington University in St. Louis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_University_in_St._Louis)___ , however, has hosted the presidential debates (organized by the ___E:Commission on Presidential Debates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_on_Presidential_Debates)___ ) three times (in 1992, 2000, and 2004), more than any other location prior to 2016, and also hosted one of the 2016 debates.

The university was also scheduled to host a debate in 1996, but it was later negotiated between the two presidential candidates to reduce the number of debates from three to two. The university hosted the only ___E:2008 vice presidential U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_debates)___ debate, as well.

___E:Hofstra University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hofstra_University)___ , originally an alternate site, was named the host of the first presidential debate in 2016, after ___E:Wright State University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wright_State_University)___ withdrew with eight weeks remaining.
This positioned Hofstra to be the only school to host presidential debates in three consecutive campaign cycles.

Most of the presidential/vice presidential debates have been moderated by ___E:ABC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_(United_States))___ , ___E:CBS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS_News)___ , ___E:CNN U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN)___ , ___E:FOX U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_News)___ , ___E:NBC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC_News)___ , and/or ___E:PBS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PBS)___ .
PBS currently holds the record for the most debates at 16.

The ___E:first presidential debate of 2024 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Joe_Biden%E2%80%93Donald_Trump_presidential_debate)___ , between ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ and ___E:Joe Biden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden)___ , was the earliest presidential debate in American history, occurring on June 27, before either candidate was officially nominated.

Biden's performance was widely criticized, a factor in his decision to ___E:end his campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Withdrawal_of_Joe_Biden_from_the_2024_United_States_presidential_election)___ .

Some of the debates can feature the candidates standing behind their podiums, or in conference tables with the moderator on the other side. Depending on the agreed format, either the moderator or an audience member can be the one to ask questions.
Typically there are no opening statements, just closing statements.
A coin toss determines who gets to answer the first question and who will make their closing remarks first.
Each candidate will get alternate turns.
Once a question is asked, the candidate has 2 minutes to answer the question.
After this, the opposing candidate has around 1 minute to respond and rebut her/his arguments.
At the moderator's discretion, the discussion of the question may be extended by 30 seconds per candidate.

In recent debates, colored lights resembling traffic lights have been installed to aid the candidate as to the time left with green indicating 30 seconds, yellow indicating 15 seconds and red indicating only 5 seconds are left. If necessary, a buzzer may be used or a flag.
Control of the presidential debates has been a ground of struggle for more than two decades.

The role was filled by the nonpartisan ___E:League of Women Voters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Women_Voters)___ (LWV) civic organization in 1976, 1980 and 1984.  In 1987, the LWV withdrew from debate sponsorship, in protest of the major party candidates attempting to dictate nearly every aspect of how the debates were conducted.
On October 2, 1988, the LWV's 14 trustees voted unanimously to pull out of the debates, and on October 3 they issued a press release:
The League of Women Voters is withdrawing sponsorship of the presidential debates...because the demands of the two campaign organizations would perpetrate a fraud on the American voter.
It has become clear to us that the candidates' organizations aim to add debates to their list of campaign-trail charades devoid of substance, spontaneity and answers to tough questions.
The League has no intention of becoming an accessory to the hoodwinking of the American public.
According to the LWV, they pulled out because "the campaigns presented the League with their debate agreement on September 28, two weeks before the scheduled debate.
The campaigns' agreement was negotiated 'behind closed doors' ... [with] 16 pages of conditions not subject to negotiation.

Most objectionable to the League...were conditions in the agreement that gave the campaigns unprecedented control over the proceedings.... [including] control the selection of questioners, the composition of the audience, hall access for the press and other issues."

The same year the two major political parties assumed control of organizing presidential debates through the ___E:Commission on Presidential Debates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_on_Presidential_Debates)___ (CPD).

The commission has been headed since its inception by former chairs of the ___E:Democratic National Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_National_Committee)___ and ___E:Republican National Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_National_Committee)___ .

Some have criticized the exclusion of ___E:third party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_party_(United_States))___ and ___E:independent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_(politician))___ candidates as contributing to lower results for candidates such as the ___E:Libertarian Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian_Party_(United_States))___ or the ___E:Green Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Party_(United_States))___ .
Others criticize the parallel interview format as a minimum of getting 15 percent in opinion polls of the CPD's choosing is required to be invited.

In 2004, the ___E:Citizens' Debate Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizens%27_Debate_Commission)___ (CDC) was formed with the stated mission of returning control of the debates to an independent nonpartisan body rather than a bipartisan body. Nevertheless, the CPD retained control of the debates that year and in 2008.
In 2024, the Democratic and Republican parties opted out of the CPD debates, in favor of debates in June and September produced by CNN and ABC News respectively.

They later agreed to a vice presidential debate in October, which would be hosted by CBS News. All three debates were conducted with no audience or outside press, but would be made available to other broadcasters.

The RNC had withdrew from the CPD in 2022 because they felt it "[was] biased and has refused to enact simple and common-sense reforms to help ensure fair debates, including hosting debates before voting begins and selecting moderators who have never worked for candidates on the debate stage."  ___E:Joe Biden campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden_2024_presidential_campaign)___ manager ___E:Jen O'Malley Dillon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jen_O%27Malley_Dillon)___ stated that the debates had become too much of a "spectacle", the CPD was not consistently enforcing its rules in prior debates, and that the debates' timetable did not end before the start of early voting.
This marked the first time the CPD had not sponsored a presidential debate since 1988.
